name: Fractal vault deposit at a stale token price before a public catch-up compute
summary: The Fractal vault prices USDF by a daily schedule that _compute advances at most 30 days per call, while deposit mints at whatever price that leaves and compute() is public. With the vault months behind, an attacker deposited 15k flash-loaned USDC.e at the lagging price, called compute() until the price was current and withdrew 1.1k USDC.e more; a copycat repeated it three blocks later, and in May 2026 another attacker did the same with 1.4M USDC.e for 14.8k.
notes: The anchor is the first deposit-then-compute withdrawal with a profit, found by tracing every deposit and compute call since the upgrade; the same sender's contract deployment 21 blocks earlier (ref) reverted. The DeFiHackLabs lead (May 2026, 0x20db7891) is a later exploit of the same defect.
The upgrade of 2023-09 re-pointed the proxy to the implementation it already ran (rule 7); later changes are an ownership transfer and compute's live period records.
